blocks.md: LATERAL = correlated subquery in FROM. Execution: for each left row, evaluate right subquery with left row's values as parameters. Index on (partition_col, order_col) enables index seek + LIMIT per left row.

blocks.label: lateral execution model
blocks.code:
-- For each employee, get latest order
SELECT e.name, o.order_date, o.total
FROM employees e
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT order_date, total
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.emp_id = e.id
  ORDER BY o.order_date DESC
  LIMIT 1
) o ON true;

-- Equivalent correlated subquery (harder to optimize)
SELECT e.name,
  (SELECT order_date FROM orders o WHERE o.emp_id = e.id ORDER BY order_date DESC LIMIT 1) AS latest_date,
  (SELECT total FROM orders o WHERE o.emp_id = e.id ORDER BY order_date DESC LIMIT 1) AS latest_total
FROM employees e;

-- LATERAL is PostgreSQL standard
-- Execution: nested loop with parameterized subquery

sections.title: Recursive CTE Internals — Working Table Iteration

blocks.md:
PostgreSQL recursive CTE uses working table / recursive table iteration:
1. Evaluate anchor query → initial working table
2. While working table not empty:
   a. Run recursive query using working table as input
   b. Result → next working table
   c. Append to recursive table
   d. Working table = next working table
3. Return recursive table
Each iteration processes one 'level' of recursion.

blocks.label: recursive cte execution
blocks.code:
-- WITH RECURSIVE paths AS (
--   SELECT id, ARRAY[id] AS path FROM nodes WHERE parent_id IS NULL
--   UNION ALL
--   SELECT n.id, p.path || n.id FROM nodes n JOIN paths p ON n.parent_id = p.id
-- )
-- EXPLAIN shows:
-- CTE Scan on paths
--   -> WorkTable Scan on paths
--       -> CTE paths
--           -> Recursive Union
--               -> Seq Scan on nodes (anchor)
--               -> WorkTable Scan on paths (recursive)
--                   -> Hash Join (nodes ⋈ paths)

-- Monitor with: EXPLAIN ANALYZE
blocks.pg: -- Recursive CTE uses WorkTable / Recursive Table iteration
blocks.py-pandas:
# Iterative approach in Python
def recursive_cte(anchor, recursive_fn, max_iter=100):
    working = anchor
    results = anchor.copy()
    for _ in range(max_iter):
        if working.empty: break
        next_working = recursive_fn(working)
        if next_working.empty: break
        results = pd.concat([results, next_working])
        working = next_working
    return results

items.explain: Working table = rows produced in previous iteration only. Recursive table accumulates all results.
Iteration stops when working table is empty (no new rows generated). Max depth is safety.

blocks.label: cte cost model
blocks.code:
-- CTE Scan cost = materialization startup + scan cost
-- EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows:
--   CTE Scan on cte
--     -> CTE cte
--         -> Seq Scan on table (startup=0, total=100)
-- Startup cost = materialization cost
-- Run cost = scan cost of materialized results

-- NOT MATERIALIZED removes CTE Scan node entirely:
--   -> Seq Scan on table (with pushed predicates)
-- No materialization overhead

-- Cost parameters:
SET cte_materialization_cost = 0.0;  -- not real param, conceptual
-- Actual: startup_cost = cost to materialize

revisionCard: LATERAL: correlated subquery in FROM; index on (partition, order) + LIMIT = O(log N) per left row
Recursive CTE: working table (prev iter) → recursive table (accumulated); WorkTable Scan in EXPLAIN
CTE Scan cost: startup = materialization; run = scan; NOT MATERIALIZED removes CTE Scan
PG 17+: predicate pushdown through NOT MATERIALIZED CTEs when safe
VOLATILE functions force materialization; NOT MATERIALIZED blocked by volatile/LIMIT/multi-ref
QUALIFY (MySQL/Snowflake) = CTE filter for window functions; PG uses CTE pattern
